property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner and any newOwner, a successful transferOwnership must set owner() to newOwner; the mutant leaves owner() unchanged, so for any newOwner different from the current owner the invariant c.owner() == newOwner is violated.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): `vm.assume` rejected too many inputs (65536 allowed)

property_summary: For every caller that is not the current owner, transferOwnership must revert and leave owner unchanged; the mutant lets anyone set the owner, so for some caller/newOwner the mutant's owner differs from the reference's.

For any non-owner caller and any candidate address, transferOwnership must leave owner unchanged (only the current owner may reassign it); the mutant, having no require, lets any caller overwrite owner, so owner changes for some non-owner input.

Calling owned() from the current owner must leave the ownership unchanged (owner stays exactly the value set by the last transferOwnership), but the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender so for an owner other than the last transferred owner the invariant breaks.

For any caller, a successful call to owned() must never alter the current owner (owner before == owner after the call); the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), breaking this for some caller.
For any caller distinct from the current owner, a successful call to owned() must leave c.owner() exactly unchanged; the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender, violating this for any such caller.

After the current owner calls transferOwnership(x), any subsequent successful owned() call by the owner must leave owner equal to x (ownership changes only via transferOwnership); the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), breaking this.

Ownership may only ever be set through transferOwnership: for any admissible caller a and any new owner x, once the current owner transfers ownership to x, any subsequent successful call to owned() (which requires msg.sender == owner) must leave c.owner() equal to x; the mutant overwrites owner with msg.sender inside owned(), so for inputs where msg.sender != the transferred-to owner the rule is broken.
